output.brief:
The buffering problem is almost certainly the new smart-TV app version 5.2, not the CDN switch. Smart-TV 5.2 sessions stall about 5.9% of viewing time. Every other kind of client was on the new CDN during the same period, and all of them stall only 0.6–0.7%. That includes older 5.1 TV apps, web and mobile. The pattern is the same on all three ISPs, so ISP congestion doesn't explain it. The stalls started on 9 Oct, with the app release and the cutover on the same day. They began two days before the handball launch, and match nights show no extra spike. So neither the CDN nor handball demand is the driver.

Recommendation: don't send the breach notice, withhold fees or roll back to Corvane. Rolling back would not fix the problem and would damage the vendor relationship. Don't mute the alert either, because it is the only warning you have. Instead, revert 5.2's adaptive-streaming behaviour in Kestria to the 5.1 settings and pause the wider 5.2 rollout until it is fixed. Also add app-version and device breakdowns to the dashboard. Hold off on the free-month offer: the October price rise is a competing explanation for the cancellations, and I did not collect evidence on that. I am fairly confident in the app diagnosis.
